html:
Britain declared a protectorate over the southern Solomon Islands in 1893, mainly to control the labour trade to Queensland and Fiji; see blackbirding. The northern islands, except Bougainville, were added from Germany in 1899.

Its capital was Tulagi. Rule was thin: a few officers, a head tax and large coconut plantations run by companies such as Levers. Missions did most of the schooling.

The Second World War wrecked Tulagi, and the capital moved to Honiara, next to the American base. After the war the Maasina Rule movement pressed for self-rule. The protectorate ended with independence under Peter Kenilorea in 1978.
